arxiv-1910-14241.title: Dynamic Regularizer with an Informative Prior
arxiv-1910-14241.creator: Avinash Kori*, Manik Sharma
arxiv-1910-14241.description: Abstract Regularization methods, specifically those which directly alter weights like L 1 L_{1} and L 2 L_{2} , are an integral part of many learning algorithms. Both the regularizers mentioned above are formulated by assuming certain priors in the parameter space and these assumptions, in some cases, induce sparsity in the parameter space.

arxiv-2201-04774.title: Experimental observation and manipulation of optical tornado waves
arxiv-2201-04774.creator: Lai Chen, Li-Gang Wang
arxiv-2201-04774.description: Abstract We report experimental generation and manipulation of optical tornado waves (ToWs). By controlling the self-focusing length, total angular momentum, and foci deviation of ToWs, the propagation properties of optical ToWs, especially their angular velocity of the main intensity lobes, can be manipulated. We achieve controlling the accumulated rotation angle of the intensity lobes from 0 to 1100 degrees.

arxiv-2207-00664.title: University of Geneva, Geneva, Switzerland
arxiv-2207-00664.description: Abstract \nu -Flows: Conditional Neutrino Regression Matthew Leigh \star , John Andrew Raine \dagger , Knut Zoch and Tobias Golling Abstract We present \nu -Flows, a novel method for restricting the likelihood space of neutrino kinematics in high-energy collider experiments using conditional normalising flows and deep invertible neural networks.

arxiv-2305-19078.title: Mechanical structures inside proton with configurational entropy language
arxiv-2305-19078.creator: Wei Kou, Xurong Chen
arxiv-2305-19078.description: Abstract The structure of the proton remains a significant challenge within the field of Quantum Chromodynamics, with the origin of its spin and mass still lacking a satisfactory explanation. In this study, we utilize the gravitational form factor of the proton as the foundation for constructing the configurational entropy of the proton energy system.

arxiv-2410-16049.title: Dirty-Waters: Detecting Software Supply Chain Smells
arxiv-2410-16049.creator: Raphina Liu, Sofia Bobadilla, Benoit Baudry, Martin Monperrus
arxiv-2410-16049.description: Abstract Using open-source dependencies is essential in modern software development. However, this practice implies significant trust in third-party code, while there is little support for developers to assess this trust. As a consequence, attacks have been increasingly occurring through third-party dependencies. These are called software supply chain attacks.

britannica-1911-subleyras-pierre.title: Subleyras, Pierre (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-subleyras-pierre.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-subleyras-pierre.description: Article 'Subleyras, Pierre' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 25), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. Fontaine and Boccaccio his true relation to the modern era comes out; and his drawings from nature are often admirable (see one of a man draped in a heavy cloak in the British Museum). Exhausted by overwork, Subleyras tried a change to Naples, but returned to Rome at the end of a few months to die (May 28, 1749).

pmc-10498642.title: A systematic comparison of human mitochondrial genome assembly tools
pmc-10498642.creator: Nirmal Singh Mahar, Rohit Satyam, Durai Sundar, Ishaan Gupta
pmc-10498642.description: BackgroundMitochondria are the cell organelles that produce most of the chemical energy required to power the cell's biochemical reactions. Despite being a part of a eukaryotic host cell, the mitochondria contain a separate genome whose origin is linked with the endosymbiosis of a prokaryotic cell by the host cell and encode independent genomic information throughout their genomes.

pmc-11445771.title: Ceramic Filters Coated with Green Ag-Nanoparticles for Drinking Water Treatment in Rural Households of Nigeria
pmc-11445771.creator: Olukemi Aromolaran, Timothy O Ogunbode
pmc-11445771.description: A ceramic water filter (CWF) coated with plant-based nanoparticles was used as household water purifier in a rural community. Silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) were produced from the stem bark of Bridelia ferruginea plant, and their efficacy to enhance the physical, chemical, and microbial quality of raw stream water sample was determined using analytical probes and pour-plate techniques, respectively.

pmc-11504843.title: Ultrasound-Guided Venous Puncture Reduces Groin Complications in Electrophysiological Procedures
pmc-11504843.creator: Yannick Teumer, Daniel Eckart, Lyuboslav Katov, Markus Graf, Carlo Bothner, Wolfgang Rottbauer, Karolina Weinmann-Emhardt, Antonio Granata, Giulio Distefano
pmc-11504843.description: Background: In electrophysiological procedures, multiple punctures on the femoral vein can be necessary depending on the number of catheters required. The femoral vein is typically located indirectly by using its anatomical relationship to the artery as a reference. However, this conventional approach can lead to significant complications, including bleeding, peri-interventional transfusion, pseudoaneurysms, or arteriovenous fistulas.

pmc-11611853.title: Investigating generative AI models and detection techniques: impacts of tokenization and dataset size on identification of AI-generated text
pmc-11611853.creator: Haowei Hua, Co-Jiayu Yao
pmc-11611853.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Generative AI models, including ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, are increasingly significant in enhancing K–12 education, offering support across various disciplines. These models provide sample answers for humanities prompts, solve mathematical equations, and brainstorm novel ideas. Despite their educational value, ethical concerns have emerged regarding their potential to mislead students into copying answers directly from AI when completing assignments, assessments, or research papers.

pmc-11642048.title: Molecular Biology of Cancer—Interplay of Malignant Cells with Emerging Therapies
pmc-11642048.creator: Stergios Boussios, Matin Sheriff, Saak V. Ovsepian
pmc-11642048.description: ogress has been especially accelerated in recent decades due to technological and conceptual breakthroughs in various fields, such as next-generation sequencing, omics sciences, high-resolution microscopy, molecular immunology, flow cytometry, single-cell analysis and sequencing, new cell culture methods, and the development of animal models, among others [2,3,4,5].

pmc-11669083.title: n-Type Conjugated Polymers Based on Double B←N Bridged Bipyridine Unit
pmc-11669083.creator: Bin Meng, Jun Liu
pmc-11669083.description: ConspectusBoth p-type conjugated polymers and n-type conjugated polymers are required for organic optoelectronic devices, such as organic solar cells (OSCs), organic field-effect transistors (OFETs), organic thermoelectrics (OTEs), etc. The development of n-type conjugated polymers lags far behind that of the p-type counterparts in view of material diversity and optoelectronic device performance.

pmc-12094576.title: Benchmark of computational hydraulics models for open-channel flow with lateral cavities
pmc-12094576.creator: Pablo Ouro, Luis Cea, Sergio Croquer, Wenhao Dong, Orlando Garcia-Feal, Adrián Navas-Montilla, Benedict D Rogers, Tatsuhiko Uchida, Carmelo Juez
pmc-12094576.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Computational models in hydro-environmental engineering are diverse in their background formulation and span from two-dimensional depth-averaged shallow water models, to complex fully three-dimensional turbulence models resolving large-eddy simulation with surface capturing techniques, and to Lagrangian particle-based methods. This paper presents a first-of-its-kind comparison of six different computational hydraulics fluid dynamics models, namely Iber+, HO-SWM, GBVC, OpenFOAM (RANS), Hydro3D (LES) and DualSPHysics (SPH), in the prediction of mean velocities and free-surface dynamics in two benchmarks involving open-channel flows with symmetric lateral cavities.

pmc-12405255.title: A landscape review with novel criteria to evaluate microbial drivers for cancer: priorities for innovative research targeting excessive cancer mortality in sub-Saharan Africa
pmc-12405255.creator: Rebecca Toumi van Dorsten, Robert F. Breiman
pmc-12405255.description: The escalating cancer burden in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), with projected doubling of incidence and mortality by 2040, necessitates innovative, cost-effective strategies for prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. While known infectious triggers like HPV, hepatitis viruses, and H. pylori account for an estimated 28.7% of cancers in SSA, the full scope of microbially-mediated oncogenesis remains underexplored.

pmc-12535721.title: Henagliflozin Increases Serum and Salivary Levels of High-Molecular-Weight Adiponectin in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes in the Community
pmc-12535721.creator: Linxin Xu, Chunfan Niu, Yun Liu, Xiaoyu Li, Zhengqian Wang, Jianhong Yin, Mina Li, Qianqian Wu, Ming Liu, Li Sun, Minggang Xu, Jing Yang, Jin Zhang
pmc-12535721.description: PurposeTo investigate Henagliflozin’s effect on high-molecular-weight (HMW) adiponectin in serum and saliva of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) patients.Patients and MethodsThis study included 66 patients with T2DM consecutively recruited from two community health service stations in southeastern Shanxi Province between December 2023 and November 2024, along with 66 healthy individuals as the normal control group.

pmc-12653092.title: Chrononutrition in Gestational Diabetes: Toward Precision Timing in Maternal Care
pmc-12653092.creator: Viktoria Xega, Jun-Li Liu
pmc-12653092.description: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a heterogeneous disorder that compromises maternal and offspring health. Conventional medical nutrition therapy focuses on nutrient composition and caloric targets but largely omits timing and individualized biology. This narrative review synthesizes mechanistic, epidemiologic and interventional evidence linking circadian biology and meal timing (chrononutrition) to maternal glycemic control.

pmc-12824650.title: Bone marrow neutrophil progenitors suppress osteoclast formation in murine cortical and trabecular bone
pmc-12824650.creator: Tsuyoshi Isojima, Blessing Crimeen-Irwin, Narelle E McGregor, Ryan C Chai, Ingrid J Poulton, Emma C Walker, Mriga Dutt, Benjamin L Parker, Natalie A Sims
pmc-12824650.description: Key Points•Neutrophil progenitors inhibit osteoclast formation both in vivo and in vitro.•Reducing marrow neutrophil progenitors causes trabecular bone loss, and delays cortical bone maturation in the absence of inflammation. Introduction Bone marrow supports maturation of multiple immune cell types before they migrate to the circulation to defend against infection.

pmc-13032652.title: Spatial multiomics dissects the SARS-CoV-2-induced disruption of cell adhesion and immune dynamics in the human hippocampus
pmc-13032652.creator: Hui Wei, Zhongman Jin, Caiyun Zhu, Pengsheng You, Jiaping Sui, Lian Huang, Nian Liu, Wanwan Zhu, Qi Xu
pmc-13032652.description: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection is associated with neurological complications, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we used an integrated spatial multiomics approach to investigate the effects of SARS-CoV-2 on human hippocampus–entorhinal cortex (HP–EC) tissues from autopsies of individuals with severe COVID-19. Our analysis revealed a cascade of pathological events initiated by viral infection.

pmc-13161721.title: Severe Peripheral Arterial Ischemia Leading to Digital Gangrene in Mixed Connective Tissue Disease: A Case Report
pmc-13161721.creator: Manuel Esaú Tamayo-Gómez, Alfonso Sandoval, Lilian Priscilla Arjona-Bojorquez, Luis Manuel Pablos-López, María Abril Mangas-Sosa, José Emiliano González Flores
pmc-13161721.description: Mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD) is a rare systemic autoimmune disorder characterized by overlapping clinical features of systemic lupus erythematosus, systemic sclerosis, and polymyositis, in association with anti-U1 ribonucleoprotein (anti-U1-RNP) antibodies. Although vascular manifestations such as Raynaud’s phenomenon are common, severe peripheral ischemic complications are rare.

pmc-13240325.title: APOE ε4, modifiable risk factors, and dementia in community‐based older Japanese adults
pmc-13240325.creator: Masaya Kumamoto, Toshiharu Ninomiya, Yoshihiko Furuta, Mao Shibata, Tomoyuki Ohara, Jun Hata, Tetsuro Ago, Yasuyuki Taki, Tatsuya Mikami, Tetsuya Maeda, Kenjiro Ono, Masaru Mimura, Ritsuko Hanajima, Jun‐ichi Iga, Minoru Takebayashi, Yukihide Momozawa, the Japan Prospective Studies for Aging and Deme
pmc-13240325.description: INTRODUCTIONApolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 is a major genetic risk factor for dementia. We examined whether APOE ε4 genotype modified the associations between a modifiable risk factor (mRF) score and dementia in older Japanese adults.METHODSThis cross‐sectional study included 9605 community‐dwelling Japanese individuals aged ≥65 years. APOE ε4 genotype and mRF scores were assessed. Dementia was clinically diagnosed.

pmc-13320711.title: Skin capillary endothelial cells form a network of spatiotemporally conserved Ca2+ activity
pmc-13320711.creator: Anush Swaminathan, David G. Gonzalez, Catherine Matte-Martone, Fei Xu, Deandra Simpson, Jessica L. Moore, Zhongqi Lin, Ushnish Rana, David Monedero-Alonso, Julia J. Mack, Chen Yuan Kam, Valentina Greco

pmc-13360917.creator: Stephanie Lim, Byron Martina

pmc-13380216.title: Improved topical delivery of curcumin by mussel adhesive protein functionalized ethosomes for effective psoriasis treatment
pmc-13380216.creator: Jiangxiu Niu, Ming Yuan, Liye Wang, Pei Zhang, Jucai Wang, Xianming Liu
pmc-13380216.description: Psoriasis is a prevalent inflammatory skin disorder exhibiting a rapidly increasing incidence. Curcumin (Cur) serves as an effective therapeutic agent for psoriasis and is commonly administered through the cutaneous route. Nevertheless, the poor skin permeability and retention of Cur restrict its therapeutic efficacy against psoriasis.

pmc-13465656.title: Moral courage in health sciences students: a systematic review of challenges, influencing factors, and consequences
pmc-13465656.creator: Kosar Kordkatuli, Sare Manoucher, Kosar Bayat, Amirali Alizadeh, Soheyla Kalantari
pmc-13465656.description: BackgroundMoral courage is the critical bridge between ethical knowledge and ethical action in healthcare. While health sciences students often possess high moral sensitivity, they frequently struggle to act on their values due to the “theory-practice gap” and the pressures of clinical hierarchies.

pmc-13551685.title: Dissipation dynamics of fipronil in tropical paddy (Oryza sativa L.) soil: unravelling its persistence and metabolism under varying moisture regime
pmc-13551685.creator: D C Preethu, K R Ashoka, T Bhagyalakshmi, S B Yogananda, L Vijaykumar, N Kirankumar, Manjanagouda S Sannagoudar

pmc-13552033.title: Massive Subcutaneous Emphysema with Bilateral Pneumothorax and Pneumoscrotum Following Clavicle Fracture without Rib Fracture: A Rare Case Report
pmc-13552033.creator: K Dharmaraj, Arjun Ganesh, Mohan Choudhary, Kevin Lourdes, D Raja Sujith Kumar
pmc-13552033.description: Introduction:Clavicle fractures are common injuries encountered in orthopedic practice, but the combination of bilateral pneumothorax, extensive subcutaneous emphysema, and pneumoscrotum without rib fractures is rare and potentially fatal. These complications are usually accompanied by pneumomediastinum and air leak in cases of blunt chest trauma.Case Report:A 74-year-old male fell and sustained a fracture of the right clavicle and scapula.

pmc-13590772.title: A large language model-enhanced knowledge graph framework for text-implied public health policy gap screening: digital health executability, behavioral accessibility, and service-support coverage
pmc-13590772.creator: Xinyi Wang, Jiao Lu
pmc-13590772.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Screening for text-implied structural gaps in policy documents is an important component of public health policy review, particularly when implementation relies on online portals, digital identity verification, remote-care platforms, or self-service processes. However, existing text classifiers, large language model prompting methods, and retrieval-based approaches often provide document-level predictions or general explanations without explicitly representing key elements, relations, and potentially missing links in policy implementation.

pmc-13634344.title: Substance use patterns in a community sample of adult women in the United States: Alcohol, Cannabis, and other drug use
pmc-13634344.creator: Shelly F Greenfield, Allen J Bailey, Laura C Seidman, Dawn E Sugarman, Kristin N Javaras, Laura A Payne, Victoria R Votaw, Nicole A Barbaro, R Kathryn McHugh
pmc-13634344.description: AimsSubstance use is a significant public health problem among women in the United States, although limited data exist on patterns of use across different demographic groups. This cross-sectional survey study aimed to examine in adult women (1) patterns of substance use (i.e., alcohol, cannabis, other drugs, and prescription medication misuse) and (2) whether these patterns varied by age cohort.
